name: Notion
summary: An all-in-one workspace that mixes documents, wikis and databases in freely nested pages.

factors: Databases with relations, rollups, formulas and automations have no standard format
Pages nest arbitrarily and mix prose with live data
Public pages used as websites, forms and customer portals
Permissions and guest access built up page by page
Online-first: there is no complete local copy unless you export one

export.summary: A workspace export produces Markdown and CSV, or HTML. Text survives well; databases flatten into CSV files and lose what made them databases.

methods.name: Workspace export
methods.detail: Settings → General → Export all workspace content, as Markdown & CSV or HTML, with subpages and files included. Only workspace owners can run it.

methods.name: API
methods.detail: The public API returns pages and databases as structured data, which is the only way to keep relations intact. You need a script or an importer that uses it.

caveats: Relations, rollups and formulas export as static text
Comments, page history and permissions are not included
Exported file names carry long ID suffixes, and deep nesting can exceed path-length limits on Windows
Synced blocks, buttons and automations do not export

paths.verdict: Best for teams whose Notion is mostly documents and wiki pages. Note that it is source-available rather than open source.

import.summary: Outline has a built-in Notion importer that takes the export archive and rebuilds collections and nested documents, images included.

lost: Databases, which arrive as static tables at best
Public pages, which must be shared again

paths.verdict: Closest in feel, databases included. Strong for one person; read the licence note before rolling it out to a team.

import.summary: AppFlowy imports a Notion export archive, turning pages into documents and simple databases into grids. Relations and formulas come through as plain values and need rebuilding.

transfers: Simple databases, as grids and boards
lost: Fine-grained sharing and public pages as you had them

paths.verdict: For individuals who used Notion as a personal notebook and would rather have local notes and backlinks.

import.summary: There is no dedicated importer. Export Notion as Markdown, add the files to a graph and clean up: Logseq is an outliner and treats every paragraph as a block, so long documents need restructuring.

transfers: The text of your pages, as Markdown
Images and attachments, after fixing paths
Links between pages, with some repair
lost: Page layout: columns, callouts and toggles become plain blocks
Publishing pages to the web as you did in Notion
